name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), battle_ domain (battle core-table region in .object3), descriptor pathfind_step_stack accurately names a recursion step-stack used by the battle pathfinding/floodfill engines and reflects the data type (a stack/buffer). No Ghidra address residue; no embedded ID needing preservation. Verified the buffer is exactly the LIFO step-stack written by the two recursion engines and walked by the two direction-collecting readers.
purpose: Scratch LIFO recursion step-stack (working memory) shared by the two battle tile-search engines: the path-search recursion and the movement-range flood-fill recursion.
logic_summary: 256-byte BSS buffer in .object3, never load-initialized (all-zero static storage incidental; first access on every search is a write). EDI walks it as a recursion frame stack; the depth counter data_fd2_battle_pathfind_current_depth (0x60077) is INC'd on push / DEC'd on pop. Two overlaid frame layouts depending on the driving engine: (1) path-search engine fd2_pathfind_recursive_with_direction (0x4E27C) uses 8-byte frames -- EDI seeded by LEA EDI,[0x60079] in the top-level entry fd2_pathfind_to_destination (0x4E252); each push writes word[EDI]=tile x,y (+0), word[EDI+2]=CX (the +3 byte = direction code 0..3), dword[EDI+4]=tile-map addr (+4), then ADD EDI,8; retry path rewrites the previous frame's +3 direction via byte[EDI-5]; pop is SUB DI,8. (2) flood-fill engine fd2_flood_fill_movement_range_recursive (0x4E0DC) uses 7-byte frames -- push writes word[EDI]=DX (+0), byte[EDI+2]=CL (+2), dword[EDI+3]=EBX (+3), ADD EDI,7; pop is SUB DI,7. Two readers walk the 8-byte path-search frames (LEA ESI,[0x60079]; MOV AL,[ESI+3]; ADD ESI,8) for current_depth iterations to harvest the per-frame direction bytes: fd2_pathfind_count_unique_directions (0x4E3DA) counts direction transitions, and fd2_pathfind_check_destination_save_path (0x4E42B) STOSBs them into an output path buffer (ptr at 0x60073). 256 bytes bounds recursion depth (>=32 frames at the 8-byte stride).
datatype: uint8[256] (flat byte buffer; overlaid with 8-byte path-search frames or 7-byte flood-fill frames at runtime, so an honest flat byte[] rather than a struct array)
element_semantics: Raw stack bytes; no per-element scalar meaning. Frame fields by engine: path-search 8-byte frame { word tile x,y @+0; byte direction-code 0..3 @+3 (high byte of CX); dword tile-map address @+4 }; flood-fill 7-byte frame { word tile x,y @+0; byte @+2 (CL); dword tile-map address @+3 }.
comment_original_issue: Source comment block (btltab3.c lines 87-120) was accurate and detailed but misattributed the EDI seeding site: it said 'EDI is seeded with LEA EDI,[0x60079] in fd2_pathfind_check_destination_save_path (0x4E252)'. Address 0x4E252 is actually inside the top-level entry fd2_pathfind_to_destination (body 0x4E1A6-0x4E27B); fd2_pathfind_check_destination_save_path (body 0x4E401-0x4E444) is one of the two readers, not the seeder. Verified function boundaries via get_function_by_address.
notes: Verified all 4 xref'd readers and both recursion engines by disassembly: push/pop strides (8 vs 7), +3 direction byte, retry rewrite byte[EDI-5], EDI seed at 0x4E252, depth counter 0x60077, and reader loops match the (corrected) src comment exactly. is_const=false confirmed: .object3 BSS, written-before-read every search (engines store frames), so zero-bss runtime buffer (not a const table). Name kept. Ghidra plate was empty (PLATE=null) so a concise plate was created from the src conclusion (correct seeder attribution).
